projects.title: PackTherm
projects.summary: A battery thermal management design toolkit that compares cooling layouts for cylindrical-cell EV packs.
results: Cell model validated against 48 blind tests on a commercial cell from 25 °C down to −20 °C, with a median surface-temperature error of 0.65 K RMSE.
Road-trip study on a 61 kWh LG M50 pack: 39 cooling designs simulated, 23 feasible.
Liquid cooling in that study costs about 0.05 % of the energy moved, against 0.29 % for the lightest forced-air design.

projects.title: Agile Flex Optimiser
projects.summary: An optimiser that schedules a household's EV charging and home battery against 12 months of real Octopus Agile prices.
results: Annual electricity bill cut from £3,591 to £2,142 (−40 %) against charging on arrival with no battery.
3,055 kWh moved out of the 16:00–19:00 peak, and emissions down 22 %.
Keeps 92 % of the saving when it plans on a price forecast instead of the real prices.

papers.title: Phase Transition Microbeads for Thermal Energy Storage Applications
papers.venue: Recent Innovations and Developments in Mechanical Engineering (ICRIDME 2024), Lecture Notes in Mechanical Engineering, pp. 87–94
papers.summary: Palmitic acid, a phase change material, sealed inside calcium alginate shells by in-situ gelation of sodium alginate with calcium chloride, then characterised with FESEM, EDX, FTIR, XRD, DSC and TGA.
findings: Melting enthalpy of about 80 J/g at a melting point of 56 °C (DSC).

papers.title: Physics-Informed Cascade Neural Network for Reliable Prediction of CO2/H2O Co-Electrolysis in SOEC
papers.venue: International Journal of Hydrogen Energy, vol. 295, article 158778
papers.summary: A neural network for predicting how a solid oxide electrolysis cell performs when it splits steam and CO2 together into syngas. Its outputs feed into each other in the order the chemistry happens, the training balances outputs of very different sizes automatically, and a physics-based part keeps predictions within mass and energy conservation while learning hidden losses.
findings: Over 99% prediction accuracy, ahead of ANN, CNN, cascade-forward and PINN models, checked against independent experiments.
Estimates Faradaic efficiency and non-ideal heat loss that are not measured directly.
Mass-conservation residual cut from 9.02% to 3.21% (mean relative).
